title: Close Calls and Skipped Lines: The Fraught State of Organ Donation

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的外面是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60个超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最出色的球队。

I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始单词。

sentences.zh: 而且我很喜欢一锅端的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮您理解世界并充分过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅即可享受特别优惠，网址为 nytimes.com 加上 subscribe。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A major investigation from The Times has found that government pressure to perform more and more organ transplants is creating greater risk for donors
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的一项重大调查发现，政府施压要求进行越来越多的器官移植，正在给捐赠者带来更大的风险

sentences.en: and threatening the overall fairness of the system.
sentences.zh: 并威胁到整个系统的高效公平性。

sentences.en: Today, my calling, investigative reporter Brian Rosenthal on what he's uncovered.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的来宾、调查记者布莱恩·罗森塔尔将谈谈他的发现。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, July 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月30日，星期三。

sentences.en: And thank you for coming into the studio.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你来到演播室。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Tell us about how this investigation that you have now been up to for many, many months began.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲你历时好几个月的这项调查是如何开始的吧。

sentences.en: So it began when I got a vague suggestion from a source that I should look into the organ transplant system.
sentences.zh: 事情的起因是我从一个消息源那里得到一个模糊的建议，让我去调查一下器官移植系统。

sentences.en: Something presumably not on your radar.
sentences.zh: 这大概不是你平时关注的领域吧。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: And so I ended up going to this conference, the American Transplant Congress, in Philadelphia last summer.
sentences.zh: 所以我最终去了去年夏天在费城举行的美国移植大会。

sentences.en: And it was a gathering of thousands of doctors and researchers talking about all aspects of the transplant system.
sentences.zh: 那是数千名医生和研究人员的聚会，他们探讨移植系统的方方面面。

sentences.en: You know, these conferences are not the most exciting events in the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些会议并不是世界上最激动人心的活动。

sentences.en: It was a lot of minutiae, a lot of technical terMs.
sentences.zh: 里面有很多琐碎的细节，大量的专业术语。

sentences.en: But then I attended one panel that really stuck with me.
sentences.zh: 但我参加的一个专题小组讨论真正让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: The panelists were speaking in really stark terms about the dramatic failings of the transplant system.
sentences.zh: 小组成员用非常严厉的措辞谈到了移植系统面临的严重失败。

sentences.en: One panelist was talking about how we violated trust in the system.
sentences.zh: 其中一位小组成员谈到我们如何破坏了对这个系统的信任。

sentences.en: We violated transparency.
sentences.zh: 我们破坏了透明度。

sentences.en: She said, we have a system in chaos.
sentences.zh: 她说，我们的系统陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And I wanted to learn what that was about.
sentences.zh: 我想了解这到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a pretty damning assessment of a system that I think most of us, from a distance, think of as very noble.
sentences.zh: 对一个我们大多数人在远观时认为非常崇高的系统来说，这是一个相当严厉的评价。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So I started to investigate.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始展开调查。

sentences.en: I ended up embedding with two organ procurement organizations.
sentences.zh: 我最终深入参与了两个器官获取组织的工作。

sentences.en: These are the organizations that coordinate transplants.
sentences.zh: 这些是协调移植的组织。

sentences.en: And I saw a lot of good things.
sentences.zh: 我看到了很多好的一面。

sentences.en: The transplant system performs thousands of life-saving transplants every year.
sentences.zh: 移植系统每年执行成千上万例拯救生命的移植手术。

sentences.en: But pretty quickly, I also started hearing about problems in the system.
sentences.zh: 但很快，我也开始听到关于这个系统存在问题的反映。

sentences.en: Problems with both how we obtain organs and how we allocate them to recipients who need transplants.
sentences.zh: 无论是我们获取器官的方式，还是将器官分配给需要移植的受体的方式，都存在问题。

sentences.en: So at both ends, basically, of the system, the beginning and the end.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上在系统的两端，也就是开头和结尾都有问题。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in short, I learned that there are significant problems with how patients who donate their organs are treated
sentences.zh: 简而言之，我了解到，捐献器官的患者如何被对待存在严重问题

sentences.en: and also problems with the fairness of how organs are allocated to recipients.
sentences.zh: 将器官分配给受体的公平性也存在问题。

sentences.en: And I came to understand that these problems were linked.
sentences.zh: 我渐渐明白，这些问题是相互关联的。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Well, both problems come back to a push in the transplant system to increase the number of transplants.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这两个问题都归结于移植系统内部为了增加移植数量而产生的一种推动力。

sentences.en: And who's making that push?
sentences.zh: 是谁在推动这个？

sentences.en: The government.
sentences.zh: 政府。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It all started with an executive order that was issued by President Trump back in 2019.
sentences.zh: 这一切都始于特朗普总统在2019年签署的一项行政命令。

sentences.en: So in his first term.
sentences.zh: 也就是他的第一个任期内。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So for years, there has been a long waiting liSt.
sentences.zh: 多年来，一直有一份很长的等待名单。

sentences.en: There are more than 100,000 Americans right now who need a transplant.
sentences.zh: 目前有超过10万名美国人需要器官移植。

sentences.en: And so the government under President Trump's first administration really tried to tackle that problem by pushing the system to recover more organs and coordinate more transplants.
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普第一任期下的政府真的试图通过推动系统回收更多器官和协调更多移植来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Do better.
sentences.zh: 做得更好。

sentences.en: Do more.
sentences.zh: 做得更多。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest proponents of reforming the system was Trump's health secretary, Alex Azar.
sentences.zh: 而推动系统改革的坚定支持者之一，就是特朗普的卫生部长亚历克斯·阿扎尔。

sentences.en: This was personal to him.
sentences.zh: 这对他是很私人的事。

sentences.en: His father had been waiting for a kidney.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲一直在等待肾源。

sentences.en: And he had seen the system as being insufficient.
sentences.zh: 他曾认为这个系统是远远不够的。

sentences.en: And so he and President Trump ordered a number of reforMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，他和特朗普总统下令进行了多项改革。

sentences.en: And the big one was a really explicit threat to the organ procurement organizations, which arrains all these transplants,
sentences.zh: 其中最大的一项是对器官获取组织发出非常明确的威胁，这些组织负责安排所有这些移植手术，

sentences.en: saying that if you do not increase the number of transplants, you are going to lose your contract.
sentences.zh: 声称如果你们不增加移植数量，你们的合同将被取消。

sentences.en: You're not going to be able to work in this space anymore.
sentences.zh: 你们将不能再在这个领域工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a very direct threat to the existence of these groups.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对这些团体的生存构成了非常直接的威胁。

sentences.en: And so they reacted by becoming much more aggressive in pursuing organs and coordinating transplants.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的反应是，在寻找器官和协调移植方面变得更加激进。

sentences.en: So help me understand how the government's desire to kick this system into higher gear and ultimately, of course, save more lives,
sentences.zh: 所以请帮我理解，政府希望推动这个系统全速运转，并最终当然是挽救更多生命的想法，

sentences.en: how that starts to do the two things that you described a bit earlier.
sentences.zh: 是如何开始导致你刚才描述的那两个问题的。

sentences.en: And let's start with the getting of the organs since it comes first in the process.
sentences.zh: 让我们从获取器官开始，因为这在流程中是第一步。

sentences.en: So let me explain how the system works.
sentences.zh: 那我来解释一下这个系统是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: There are these organ procurement organizations that I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 有我刚才提到的这些器官获取组织。

sentences.en: They are nonprofit groups that exist in every state.
sentences.zh: 它们是在每个州存在的非营利组织。

sentences.en: And they have employees in hospitals basically looking for people who are dying and might be candidates to donate their organs.
sentences.zh: 它们的员工在医院里，基本上寻找那些正在垂死边缘且可能是器官捐献候选人的人。

sentences.en: So people who have been shooting victims or drug overdose victims or motor vehicle crashes who are in the hospital, who are nearing death,
sentences.zh: 所以那些在医院里生命垂危的枪击受害者、药物过量受害者或车祸受害者，

sentences.en: the organ procurement organizations are going to try to pursue their organs.
sentences.zh: 器官获取组织会试图获取他们的器官。

sentences.en: And there are basically two different ways that they can do that.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上可以通过两种不同的方式做到这一点。

sentences.en: The normal way, the way that happens more often, is when the patient becomes brain dead.
sentences.zh: 正常的方式，也就是更常见的方式，是患者脑死亡。

sentences.en: This is a patient who has lost all functioning in their brain permanently.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大脑功能已经永久丧失的患者。

sentences.en: It's irreversible.
sentences.zh: 这是不可逆转的。

sentences.en: It's confirmed by scientific tests.
sentences.zh: 经过科学测试确认。

sentences.en: And the organ procurement organizations can keep their organs viable on machines until they're ready for a transplant.
sentences.zh: 器官获取组织可以在机器上保持其器官有活力，直到准备好进行移植。

sentences.en: But that is really the extent of what happens in that case.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是那种情况下所发生事情的全部限度了。

sentences.en: Is that the most common form of death, at which point organs are harvested?
sentences.zh: 这是最常见的死亡形式，并在此节点上摘取器官吗？

sentences.en: It's the most common form of donation.
sentences.zh: 这是最常见的捐献形式。

sentences.en: And it used to be the only form of donation.
sentences.zh: 它曾经是唯一的捐献形式。

sentences.en: But more recently, and especially after this executive order, there has been a growing use of another type of organ donation called donation after circulatory death.
sentences.zh: 但最近，特别是在这项行政命令之后，另一种被称为循环死亡后捐献的器官捐献类型的使用越来越多。

sentences.en: Donation after circulatory death.
sentences.zh: 循环死亡后捐献。

sentences.en: And what is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: How is it different from getting an organ when someone's brain dead?
sentences.zh: 这与在患者脑死亡时获取器官有什么不同？

sentences.en: It's a totally different process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完全不同的过程。

sentences.en: So usually the patient is in a coma.
sentences.zh: 所以通常患者处于昏迷状态。

sentences.en: They have some level of brain activity.
sentences.zh: 他们有一些水平的大脑活动。

sentences.en: But a doctor has determined that they will never be able to survive without life support.
sentences.zh: 但医生已经确定，如果没有生命支持，他们将永远无法存活。

sentences.en: And so the family can authorize the withdrawal of life support in order to donate organs.
sentences.zh: 因此家属可以授权撤除生命支持以便捐献器官。

sentences.en: And if that happens, the patient is taken to an operating room.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，患者会被带到手术室。

sentences.en: The life support is withdrawn.
sentences.zh: 撤除生命支持。

sentences.en: They wait for the patient's heart to stop, which means they have died by circulatory death.
sentences.zh: 他们等待患者的心脏停止跳动，这意味着他们已经死于循环死亡。

sentences.en: And then after that, they remove the organs.
sentences.zh: 然后在此之后，他们移除器官。

sentences.en: So how has this effort from the federal government to get more organs and more transplantations been affecting this second pathway that you've just described?
sentences.zh: 那么，联邦政府为获取更多器官和更多移植所做出的这种努力，是如何影响你刚才描述的这第二条途径的呢？

sentences.en: There's been a huge increase in donation after circulatory death since these regulations came into effect.
sentences.zh: 自从这些规章生效以来，循环死亡后捐献的数量大幅增加。

sentences.en: Usage has tripled.
sentences.zh: 使用率增加了两倍。

sentences.en: And that's great for the people who have received the organs.
sentences.zh: 这对接受器官的人来说是件大好事。

sentences.en: Some 40,000 people who need a transplant have gotten one.
sentences.zh: 大约有4万名需要移植的人得到了移植。

sentences.en: But doctors say that there have also been probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但医生们表示，这也带来了问题。

sentences.en: And the reason why is that donation after circulatory death is just much less black and white than donation after brain death.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，循环死亡后捐献比脑死亡捐献要模糊得多，远非非黑即白。

sentences.en: So one of the key things with donation after circulatory death is you're supposed to identify a patient who is on life support and has no chance of recovering.
sentences.zh: 因此，循环死亡后捐献的关键点之一，是你要识别出一位靠生命支持维持且毫无康复希望的患者。

sentences.en: But that's a medical judgment call.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种医疗判断。

sentences.en: And what we have found in our reporting is that a growing number of patients who are being pursued for organ donation are actually ending up showing signs of recovering.
sentences.zh: 我们在报道中发现的是，越来越多的正被寻求器官捐献的患者实际上最终显示出了康复的迹象。

sentences.en: In other words, they were not headed for death.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们并不是在走向死亡。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: That's a really bracing thing to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到这个真是让人振奋又震惊。

sentences.en: Just explain and maybe give an example of what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下，或许可以举个例子说明你在说什么。

sentences.en: So the best-known case happened a few years ago in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 最著名的案例发生在几年前的肯塔基州。

sentences.en: It was a man who had suffered from an overdose.
sentences.zh: 那是一名因药物过量而发病的男子。

sentences.en: He had fallen into a coma.
sentences.zh: 他陷入了昏迷。

sentences.en: He was not expected to recover.
sentences.zh: 预计他无法康复。

sentences.en: And so his family had authorized the organ procurement organization to pursue his organs via this type of donation.
sentences.zh: 因此他的家属授权器官获取组织通过这种类型的捐献来获取他的器官。

sentences.en: And he was not brain dead.
sentences.zh: 而他并没有脑死亡。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And so they started testing his organs.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始测试他的器官。

sentences.en: They started lining up recipients for his organs, lining up people to do the surgery.
sentences.zh: 他们开始为他的器官排定受体，安排做手术的人。

sentences.en: And while they were doing those preparations, he started opening his eyes.
sentences.zh: 就在他们进行这些准备工作时，他开始睁开眼睛。

sentences.en: He pulled his knees to his cheSt.
sentences.zh: 他把膝盖拉向胸口。

sentences.en: And this was noted but kind of dismissed as meaningless body reflexes.
sentences.zh: 这一点被注意到了，但被当作无意义的身体反射而忽略了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so they continued moving forward.
sentences.zh: 于是他们继续推进。

sentences.en: They took him into the operating room.
sentences.zh: 他们把他带进手术室。

sentences.en: They were about to withdraw his life support, wait for him to die and take out the organs.
sentences.zh: 他们正准备撤除他的生命支持，等待他死去并取出器官。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, one of the doctors said that they were not comfortable moving forward.
sentences.zh: 突然间，其中一位医生表示他们对继续进行感到不安心。

sentences.en: And we actually have reporting that the procurement organization wanted to keep moving forward.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有报道称，获取组织希望继续推进。

sentences.en: But the doctor refused.
sentences.zh: 但医生拒绝了。

sentences.en: She put her foot down and the patient was returned to his hospital room where, unexpectedly, he recovered.
sentences.zh: 她态度坚决，患者被送回了病房，出乎意料的是，他康复了。

sentences.en: But years later, he is still alive after being minutes away from dying in the operating room.
sentences.zh: 但多年后，在距离手术室死亡仅几分钟之遥后，他依然活着。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Clearly, it's very alarming that a medical team almost withdrew this patient's life support.
sentences.zh: 显然，医疗团队差点撤除这名患者的生命支持，这是非常令人担忧的。

sentences.en: But in the end, they didn't.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他们没有这样做。

sentences.en: That seems important to highlight.
sentences.zh: 这一点似乎很重要，值得强调。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 是的，这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: So how frequently is a situation like that occurring, where they get real close to withdrawing life support, and it turns out there are signs of life?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种情况发生的频率有多高？就是他们非常接近拔掉生命支持系统，结果却发现有生命迹象的情况？

sentences.en: Well, there's no official count of that, but here's what we do know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，虽然没有官方统计，但我们了解到的情况是这样的。

sentences.en: After this case was reported, the federal government did an investigation in Kentucky, and they looked at 350 cases where plans to retrieve organs were canceled at the last moment.
sentences.zh: 在这个案例被报道后，联邦政府在肯塔基州进行了一项调查，他们查看了350个在最后关头取消器官获取计划的案例。

sentences.en: And what they found was that in 73 of those cases, they stopped at the last minute,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，在其中73个案例中，他们是在最后一分钟才停下来的，

sentences.en: but they should have stopped much sooner because the patient was showing signs of regaining consciousness sooner, and those signs were initially ignored.
sentences.zh: 但他们本该早得多停下来，因为患者早就表现出了恢复意识的迹象，而这些迹象最初被忽视了。

sentences.en: So what have you come to understand about why a group of doctors and nurses would be missing signs of life?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于为什么一群医生和护士会错过生命迹象，你有什么样的了解？

sentences.en: I keep thinking about any time I've been in a hospital, and there are machines after machines on the wall telling you about people's vital signs.
sentences.zh: 我一直在想，每次我去医院，墙上都有密密麻麻的机器向你显示人们的生命体征。

sentences.en: So this seems a little hard to understand.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎有点难以理解。

sentences.en: Well, the vital signs are staying consistent because they're on ventilators, they're on machines.
sentences.zh: 嗯，生命体征保持一致是因为他们连着呼吸机，连着各种机器。

sentences.en: You're really looking for signs of brain activity.
sentences.zh: 你真正要寻找的是脑部活动的迹象。

sentences.en: And it turns out that can be quite subtle.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这可能非常微弱微妙。

sentences.en: And so, yes, doctors are supposed to be looking for these signs, but instead of doing that, once the patient has been authorized for organ donation,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，医生本该寻找这些迹象，但事实并非如此，一旦患者被批准捐献器官，

sentences.en: the system kind of sees them as an organ donor.
sentences.zh: 这个系统在某种程度上就把他们视为器官捐献者了。

sentences.en: They put on blinders.
sentences.zh: 他们戴上了眼罩。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: We talked to nurses, doctors, organ procurement employees, all around the country, who all said that this system is not working as well as it should.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了全国各地的护士、医生、器官获取机构员工，他们都表示这个系统的运转情况没有达到应有的水平。

sentences.en: And we confirmed a dozen cases in which patients endured either premature or bungled attempts to retrieve their organs.
sentences.zh: 我们核实了十几起患者遭遇过早或拙劣的器官获取尝试的案例。

sentences.en: Separate from those in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 不包括肯塔基州的那些。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: In nine other states, different types of patients, and different types of mistakes.
sentences.zh: 在其他九个州，不同类型的患者，以及不同类型的错误。

sentences.en: I mean, how should we think about this?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们该如何看待这件事？

sentences.en: Because at the end of the day, these almost horrifying outcomes were averted.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，这些几乎骇人听闻的结局是被避免了。

sentences.en: We don't know, and maybe it's not knowable, whether anyone had their life support withdrawn when they might have made a full recovery.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道，也许也无法知道，是否有人在本来可能完全康复的情况下被拔掉了生命支持。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: I think it's impossible to know.
sentences.zh: 我认为不可能知道。

sentences.en: But I can say that we did speak with a lot of doctors and nurses who felt that that has happened.
sentences.zh: 但我可以说，我们确实和许多感觉这种事已经发生的医生和护士交谈过。

sentences.en: And they say, given how much this donation type has increased in the last few years and the subjectivity, they think it's hard to imagine that this has not happened.
sentences.zh: 他们说，鉴于这种捐献类型在过去几年里大幅增加，而且存在主观性，他们认为很难想象这种事没有发生过。

sentences.en: And how much do all the folks that you've spoken to who are involved in this attribute what you're describing to the federal government asking, demanding really, more organs?
sentences.zh: 那么，你所交谈过的所有参与其中的人，在多大程度上将你所描述的情况归咎于联邦政府要求、甚至是强烈要求获得更多器官？

sentences.en: Almost everybody blames those regulations.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都指责这些规定。

sentences.en: They say that ever since they've gone into effect, the organ procurement organizations have become very aggressive, that they want to get as many organs as possible,
sentences.zh: 他们说，自从这些规定生效以来，器官获取组织变得非常激进，他们想尽可能多地获取器官，

sentences.en: they want to save lives, and that as a result, they're pushing the limits.
sentences.zh: 他们想要拯救生命，而结果就是，他们在突破极限。

sentences.en: Good intentions, in this case, they seem to be saying, are leading to greater risk.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎在说，这种情况下，好意却带来了更大的风险。

sentences.en: And remember, that is only the first half of the problem.
sentences.zh: 记住，这只是问题的前半部分。

sentences.en: But our reporting also found that these regulations have had an effect on the fairness of who gets all of these organs.
sentences.zh: 但我们的报道还发现，这些规定对谁能获得所有这些器官的公平性产生了影响。

sentences.en: Which is what we're going to talk about after the break.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们休息之后要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏部门拼字游戏 Connections 的创作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马苏尔斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天创作 Spelling Bee 和 Letterboxd 游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的状况。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: So, Brian, explain how these pressures from the federal government to get more organs,
sentences.zh: 那么，布赖恩，请解释一下联邦政府要求获取更多器官的这些压力——

sentences.en: which you've already described as influencing the first half of this process, the getting of the organs, how they have exerted pressure on the second half,
sentences.zh: 你刚才已经将其描述为影响了这个过程的前半部分，也就是获取器官的过程——它们是如何对后半部分施加压力的，

sentences.en: the process of placing organs into the patients who need them.
sentences.zh: 也就是将器官移植给需要的患者的过程。

sentences.en: So, basically, these regulations have led the procurement organizations to try to allocate as many organs as quickly as they can.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，这些规定导致获取组织试图尽可能快地分配尽可能多的器官。

sentences.en: And that has led them to look for ways to cut corners and to not follow the rules.
sentences.zh: 这导致他们寻找走捷径和不遵守规则的方法。

sentences.en: So, you've probably heard of the organ waiting list, but there actually is not one official list of everybody in the country who needs an organ.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能听说过器官等待名单，但实际上全国并没有一个官方的、包含所有需要器官的人的名单。

sentences.en: It's not like you're number 1,000 today and you'll be number 999 tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 它不像你今天排第1,000名，明天就会排第999名那样。

sentences.en: There is a pool of people who need an organ.
sentences.zh: 存在的是一个需要器官的人群库。

sentences.en: And every time an organ becomes available, there is a unique list that is generated for that organ of the people who, first of all, are the best match,
sentences.zh: 每当有器官可用时，都会为该器官生成一份独特的名单，名单上的人首先是最合适的匹配者，

sentences.en: who are the right size, who are the right blood type, who are close by, and also who have been deemed by the system to be most deserving of that organ.
sentences.zh: 体型合适、血型正确、距离较近，并且也被系统认为是最应获得该器官的人。

sentences.en: And how is that determination made?
sentences.zh: 这个决定是如何做出的？

sentences.en: It's an algorithm, and the biggest factors are how long you've been waiting and how sick you are.
sentences.zh: 这是一个算法，最大的因素是你等待的时间有多长以及你的病情有多严重。

sentences.en: Seems pretty straightforward.
sentences.zh: 听起来挺直截了当的。

sentences.en: Basically, any time an organ, a liver, a kidney, a heart becomes available, you're saying the system creates this smaller list from the pool you just described.
sentences.zh: 基本上，每当有器官——肝脏、肾脏、心脏——可用时，你是说系统会从你刚才描述的人群库中创建这个较小的名单？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so, once that smaller list for that specific organ is created, it is the job of the procurement organization to go down the list,
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦为那个特定的器官创建了较小的名单，获取组织的工作就是顺着名单往下找，

sentences.en: starting with the very first person on the list, and it's spelled out actually how they do that.
sentences.zh: 从名单上的第一个人开始，而且具体怎么做是有明确规定的。

sentences.en: They don't contact the patient.
sentences.zh: 他们不联系患者。

sentences.en: They contact the patient's doctor.
sentences.zh: 他们联系患者的医生。

sentences.en: The patient's doctor has 30 minutes to respond yes or no.
sentences.zh: 患者的医生有30分钟的时间做出是或否的回应。

sentences.en: If they say no, which does happen, the procurement organization is supposed to go to the second person on the list and make that offer.
sentences.zh: 如果他们说不（这种情况确实会发生），获取组织应该去找名单上的第二个人并提供该器官。

sentences.en: They've got 30 minutes to respond.
sentences.zh: 他们有30分钟时间回应。

sentences.en: Then they go to the next person.
sentences.zh: 然后他们去找下一个人。

sentences.en: And the underlying principle of all of this is fairness, which is extremely important to the system.
sentences.zh: 这一切的根本原则是公平，这对系统来说极其重要。

sentences.en: I mean, you can imagine if we didn't have rules, the best heart could go to the wealthiest donor to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以想象，如果我们没有规则，最好的心脏可能会给医院最富有的捐赠者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: The member of the board.
sentences.zh: 董事会成员。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: It's also worth noting that following these steps is federally required.
sentences.zh: 还值得注意的是，遵循这些步骤是联邦法律要求的。

sentences.en: These steps are spelled out in regulations.
sentences.zh: 这些步骤在规章制度中有明确规定。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, back to our thesis here.
sentences.zh: 那么，回到我们的核心论点。

sentences.en: How has this new push from the federal government to do more in this space influenced the fairness of this all?
sentences.zh: 联邦政府在这方面的新推动力，是如何影响这一切的公平性的？

sentences.en: So, instead of calling number one on the list, taking the chance that they say no, then having to call the next person, maybe they'll say no,
sentences.zh: 所以，与其给名单上的第一个人打电话、承担他们说不的风险，然后不得不给下一个人打电话、对方可能也会说不，

sentences.en: instead of waiting and going through that process, they have come up with a new plan called out-of-sequence allocation,
sentences.zh: 与其等待并经历那个过程，他们想出了一个新计划，叫做顺序外分配（out-of-sequence allocation），

sentences.en: which is when they simply call up a hospital that they have a relationship with and say, hey, we have an organ.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们直接给有合作关系的医院打电话说，嘿，我们有一个器官。

sentences.en: You can put it into any one of your patients.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它移植给你们的任何一个患者。

sentences.en: And what did you find in your reporting about how frequently this alternative process is happening?
sentences.zh: 你在报道中发现这种替代流程发生的频率如何？

sentences.en: So, today, nearly 20% of organs do not go to the people at the top of the liSt.
sentences.zh: 如今，近20%的器官没有流向名单顶端的人。

sentences.en: And back in 2020, it was only 3%.
sentences.zh: 而在2020年，这一比例仅为3%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I heard many, many stories about people being skipped over.
sentences.zh: 我听到了很多很多关于人们被跳过的故事。

sentences.en: And one that really stuck with me was about a teenager named Marcus who lives in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 其中一个让我印象深刻的故事是关于一个名叫马库斯（Marcus）的密歇根州少年的。

sentences.en: Marcus has been fighting kidney trouble his whole life.
sentences.zh: 马库斯一生都在与肾病作斗争。

sentences.en: He'd been waiting for nearly a decade for a transplant.
sentences.zh: 他已经等待移植将近十年了。

sentences.en: And he had a unique medical condition, which meant that he was not a match for very many organs.
sentences.zh: 他有一种独特的身体状况，这意味着他与绝大多数器官都不匹配。

sentences.en: And then last spring, his doctor called to say that there was a match.
sentences.zh: 然后去年春天，他的医生打电话说有了一个匹配的器官。

sentences.en: He was on the top of the liSt.
sentences.zh: 他排在名单的顶端。

sentences.en: This kidney had been in Illinois.
sentences.zh: 这个肾脏当时在伊利诺伊州。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be used in another procedure, but that had fallen through.
sentences.zh: 它本应用在另一台手术中，但那台手术泡汤了。

sentences.en: And so Marcus was next up.
sentences.zh: 所以轮到马库斯了。

sentences.en: He and his family were really excited.
sentences.zh: 他和他的家人非常兴奋。

sentences.en: They rushed to his hospital in Michigan to prepare for the surgery.
sentences.zh: 他们冲向密歇根州的医院为手术做准备。

sentences.en: But the kidney did not go to him that night.
sentences.zh: 但那天晚上肾脏没有给他。

sentences.en: It didn't go to the next person on the list or the next person after that.
sentences.zh: 它没有给名单上的下一个人，也没有给接下来的那个人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That very much sounds like a list being ignored, skipped.
sentences.zh: 这听起来非常像一份名单被忽视了、被跳过了。

sentences.en: So what did you find actually happened there?
sentences.zh: 那么你发现那里实际发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the procurement organization, knowing that the kidney was already at the University of Illinois,
sentences.zh: 嗯，获取组织知道肾脏已经伊利诺伊大学了，

sentences.en: ended up saying to that hospital, hey, why don't you keep it?
sentences.zh: 最后对那家医院说，嘿，你们为什么不留着它呢？

sentences.en: Just give it to whichever patient you want.
sentences.zh: 随便把它给你们想要的哪个患者都行。

sentences.en: And they ended up putting the kidney into a patient who had only been waiting for a few months.
sentences.zh: 他们最终把肾脏移植给了一个只等待了几个月的患者。

sentences.en: They were number 3,558 on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 他在名单上排在第3,558位。

sentences.en: That's stunning, and I want to better understand it.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了，我想更好地了解一下。

sentences.en: In your reporting, did you come to the conclusion that the procurement organization was worried, for instance, that transporting this kidney from Illinois to Michigan
sentences.zh: 在你的报道中，你是否得出结论认为，获取组织担心，例如，将这个肾脏从伊利诺伊州运送到密歇根州

sentences.en: was going to take so long that the kidney would deteriorate?
sentences.zh: 会花太长时间以至于肾脏会变质？

sentences.en: I mean, was a factor like that at play?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是否有这样的因素在起作用？

sentences.en: So they said they had to place this kidney quickly, that kidneys are only viable outside the body for a certain amount of time,
sentences.zh: 所以他们说他们必须快速安置这个肾脏，肾脏在体外只能存活一定的时间，

sentences.en: which didn't really seem like a reasonable explanation.
sentences.zh: 这听起来似乎并不是一个合理的解释。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, Illinois is not that far away from Michigan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，伊利诺伊州离密歇根州并不算太远。

sentences.en: The kidney had only been outside the body for about 9 or 10 hours at that point, and kidneys remained viable for up to 48 hours.
sentences.zh: 那时肾脏在体外才大约9到10个小时，而肾脏最长可以存活48小时。

sentences.en: And so they had plenty of time to send that kidney down the road.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有充足的时间把那个肾脏送过去。

sentences.en: In fact, Marcus's doctor had even called and offered that he would drive down and pick it up himself.
sentences.zh: 事实上，马库斯的医生甚至打电话主动提出自己开车去把它取回来。

sentences.en: Wow, from Michigan to Illinois to get it from Marcus.
sentences.zh: 哇，从密歇根到伊利诺伊去为马库斯取肾。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the OPO had decided that they just wanted to give it to the University of Illinois and be done with it.
sentences.zh: 但OPO决定他们只想把它给伊利诺伊大学，然后就了事。

sentences.en: So that makes me wonder, what if any ramifications are there for a procurement organization like this one that breaks the federal rules, skips the line over someone like Marcus,
sentences.zh: 这让我想知道，像这样一个违反联邦规则、跳过像马库斯这样的人的排队规则的器官获取组织，会有什么后果吗？

sentences.en: does it face any consequences?
sentences.zh: 它会面临任何惩罚吗？

sentences.en: So every time there's a violation, the case is flagged for review.
sentences.zh: 所以每次有违规行为，这个案例都会被标记以供审查。

sentences.en: But what we found in our reporting is that basically nobody ever gets in trouble for this.
sentences.zh: 但我们在报道中发现的是，基本上从来没有人会因此惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: More than 99.5% of the time, the case is closed without any action.
sentences.zh: 超过99.5%的情况下，案件在没有任何行动的情况下就被结案了。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that the transplant system basically polices itself.
sentences.zh: 原因在于移植系统基本上是在自我监管。

sentences.en: And it has no incentive to penalize one of its own members.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何动力去惩罚自己的成员。

sentences.en: What was the reaction from Marcus's family to this sequence of events that you just described?
sentences.zh: 马库斯的家人对你刚才描述的一系列事件有什么反应？

sentences.en: Well, they didn't know about all that information I just told you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不知道我刚告诉你的所有这些信息。

sentences.en: They knew that they didn't get the transplant, but they didn't know that they'd been skipped.
sentences.zh: 他们知道自己没有得到移植，但他们不知道自己被跳过了。

sentences.en: And so I went to their house and met with them and told them everything that we knew.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了他们家，和他们见了面，把我们所知道的一切都告诉了他们。

sentences.en: It was heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 这太令人心碎了。

sentences.en: And we told them where that kidney had ultimately gone to.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉了他们那个肾脏最终去了哪里。

sentences.en: And the family was just devastated.
sentences.zh: 家属简直悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: Marcus's mom actually said to me, what made them decide that Marcus wasn't good enough for that kidney?
sentences.zh: 马库斯的妈妈甚至对我说，是什么让他们觉得马库斯不配得到那个肾脏？

sentences.en: For everyone in Marcus's family, this is just very hard to make sense of.
sentences.zh: 对马库斯家里的每个人来说，这都很难理解。

sentences.en: How is Marcus now?
sentences.zh: 马库斯现在怎么样？

sentences.en: So Marcus was ultimately able to get a transplant.
sentences.zh: 所以马库斯最终还是能够进行移植。

sentences.en: A couple months after this all happened, he did get a kidney, but it was not as good of a kidney.
sentences.zh: 这一切发生几个月后，他确实得到了一个肾脏，但那不是一个那么好的肾脏。

sentences.en: It came from somebody who was older that wasn't as perfect of a match.
sentences.zh: 它来自一个年纪更大、匹配度不是那么完美的人。

sentences.en: As the one he didn't get.
sentences.zh: 比他没能得到的那个差。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: And so that kidney is not doing so well.
sentences.zh: 所以那个肾脏情况不太好。

sentences.en: In fact, it's not really functioning at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它几乎完全无法运作。

sentences.en: And he is going to have to get back on the transplant list and wait for a new one.
sentences.zh: 他将不得不重新回到移植名单上，等待一个新的肾脏。

sentences.en: That's really heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 这真的太让人心碎了。

sentences.en: Brian, putting aside for just a moment the specifics of this kidney and of Marcus, is there evidence that when procurement organizations skip the line,
sentences.zh: 布赖恩，抛开这枚肾脏和马库斯的具体情况不谈，有没有证据表明，当器官采购组织插队时，

sentences.en: they're more effective at getting organs placed in patients?
sentences.zh: 他们在把器官分配给患者方面更有效率？

sentences.en: No, there is not.
sentences.zh: 不，并没有。

sentences.en: In the transplant system, there is a closely watched metric called the discard rate, which is the percentage of organs that are recovered that do not end up getting transplanted.
sentences.zh: 在移植系统中，有一个备受关注的指标叫作废弃率，也就是被回收但最终未能用于移植的器官所占的百分比。

sentences.en: And you would expect that if the skipping the line is so effective at getting more organs placed, then the discard rate would be going down.
sentences.zh: 你本会认为，如果插队在促成更多器官移植方面如此有效，那么废弃率应该在下降。

sentences.en: And that is not happening.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: The national discard rate is not going down.
sentences.zh: 全国的器官废弃率并没有下降。

sentences.en: And in fact, the procurement organizations that are skipping the list the most do not have a lower discard rate than the ones that are not skipping the list as much.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那些最常插队的器官采购组织，其废弃率并不比那些不怎么插队的组织低。

sentences.en: And it also leads to some measurable bias.
sentences.zh: 而且这也导致了一些可度量的偏见。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: Well, when procurement organizations skipped the list, our reporting found that organs disproportionately go to white men, to Asians, and to people with college degrees.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当器官采购组织插队时，我们的报道发现，器官不成比例地流向了白人男性、亚正如一位医生对我说的那样，这就是为什么我们要制定政策来消除这些偏见，确保系统是公平的。

sentences.en: As one doctor put it to me, this is why we have policies in place to root out these biases and make sure that the system is fair.
sentences.zh: 正如一位医生对我说的那样，这就是为什么我们要制定政策来根除这些偏见并确保系统是公平的。

sentences.en: I'm curious what the federal government's response has been to your investigation.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道联邦政府对你们的调查作出了什么回应。

sentences.en: Because what the reporting clearly demonstrates is that the actions of the first Trump administration is encouraging these procurement organizations
sentences.zh: 因为报道清楚地表明，特朗普第一任期的行动鼓励了这些器官采购组织

sentences.en: to increasingly ignore the lines and be much more aggressive with how they're trying to procure the organs.
sentences.zh: 越来越忽视排队规则，在试图采购器官时变得更加激进。

sentences.en: And since Trump is now president again, are you finding that the regulators working for him are defensive of the system?
sentences.zh: 既然特朗普现在又当回了总统，你们发现为他工作的监管机构在为这个系统辩护吗？

sentences.en: Or are they open to the idea that the actions they took in the first term have now created a set of problems?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们愿意承认，他们在第一任期采取的行动现在引发了一系列问题？

sentences.en: The Trump administration has been very responsive to our findings on both of these issues.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府对我们在这两个问题上的调查结果反应非常积极。

sentences.en: When we contacted them about the issue of line skipping, they immediately sent a letter to the transplant system saying that this was a big problem
sentences.zh: 当我们就插队问题联系他们时，他们立即向移植系统发送了一封信，称这是一个大问题，

sentences.en: and that new policies needed to be written to address these issues.
sentences.zh: 并且需要制定新政策来解决这些问题。

sentences.en: And as for the aggressively procuring organs from donation after circulatory death, they have cracked down on the procurement organization in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 至于从心跳停止后的捐赠中积极采购器官的做法，他们已经对肯塔基州的器官采购组织进行了打击。

sentences.en: And they have ordered the transplant system to write new guidelines around donation after circulatory death nationwide.
sentences.zh: 他们还下令移植系统在全国范围内围绕心跳停止后的捐赠编写新的指导方针。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: They're taking it very seriously.
sentences.zh: 他们非常认真地对待这件事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're being pushed to take it very seriously by Congress.
sentences.zh: 而且他们正受到国会的推动，必须非常严肃地对待此事。

sentences.en: The Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations will now come to order.
sentences.zh: 监督与调查小组委员会现在开会。

sentences.en: So last week in the House, there was a hearing of the committee that oversees the transplant system.
sentences.zh: 因此，上周在众议院，监督移植系统的委员会举行了一场听证会。

sentences.en: The New York Times has written on chaos in the waiting liSt.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》曾撰文报道等待名单上的混乱状况。

sentences.en: And lawmakers in both parties were mentioning or reporting.
sentences.zh: 两党议员都在提及或报道。

sentences.en: A recent investigative report highlighting one of the most horrific cases of patient abuses.
sentences.zh: 一份最近的调查报道重点关注了最骇人听闻的患者虐待案例之一。

sentences.en: We're asking hard questions of the transplant system officials.
sentences.zh: 我们正在向移植系统官员提出尖锐的问题。

sentences.en: Were those protocols in place?
sentences.zh: 这些规程当时到位了吗？

sentences.en: They were.
sentences.zh: 是的，到位了。

sentences.en: And why were they not followed?
sentences.zh: 那为什么没有遵循它们？

sentences.en: And we're calling for reform.
sentences.zh: 我们正在呼吁改革。

sentences.en: If you see a patient crying, if you see these kind of neurologic responses, the process should be immediately stopped.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到患者在哭泣，如果你看到这种神经系统反应，这个过程应该立即停止。

sentences.en: Do you agree?
sentences.zh: 你同意吗？

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: You know, it strikes me that a lot of people listening to this conversation are going to remember, as I have,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我突然想到，许多听到这段对话的人会和我一样回想起，

sentences.en: that I'm an organ donor.
sentences.zh: 我是一名器官捐献者。

sentences.en: I mean, I have it right here on my driver's license, the heart.
sentences.zh: 我的驾照上就有这个心形标志。

sentences.en: A lot of us are organ donors, proudly.
sentences.zh: 我们当中有很多人都是器官捐献者，而且为此感到自豪。

sentences.en: And in becoming an organ donor, we have entrusted ourselves, our organs, perhaps even the process by which our life ultimately ends, to the system that you have been investigating.
sentences.zh: 而在成为器官捐献者的过程中，我们把自己、我们的器官，甚至可能是我们生命最终走向终点的过程，托付给了你们一直在调查的这个系统。

sentences.en: So, should what you have found here
sentences.zh: 那么，你们在这里发现的情况，

sentences.en: change how we think about that decision, being an organ donor?
sentences.zh: 是否应该改变我们对成为器官捐献者这一决定的看法？

sentences.en: I think that being an organ donor is a beautiful gift.
sentences.zh: 我认为成为器官捐献者是一份美丽的礼物。

sentences.en: And the whole system is based on that act of giving.
sentences.zh: 而整个系统正是建立在那种奉献行为之上的。

sentences.en: It's a system that saves thousands of lives every year.
sentences.zh: 这是一个每年拯救成千上万条生命的系统。

sentences.en: But, you know, as we've talked about today, the system is also under strain.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如我们今天所讨论的，这个系统也承受着压力。

sentences.en: And it seems like this is a rare issue where there is bipartisan support toward the idea that something needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 而且这似乎是一个罕见的问题，各方在必须采取行动这一想法上有着跨党派的支持。

sentences.en: And it's never going to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 它永远不可能是完美的。

sentences.en: This is a system that will always have people making tough decisions under pressure.
sentences.zh: 这是一个永远都会有人在压力下做出艰难决定的系统。

sentences.en: But we'll see if these fixes can help.
sentences.zh: 但我们将拭目以待，看这些修复措施能否有所帮助。

sentences.en: Because what everybody wants is to honor that tremendous gift of organ donation.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都希望尊重器官捐献那份巨大的馈赠。

sentences.en: Well, Brian, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，布赖恩，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: The gunman who killed four people in a midtown
sentences.zh: 周一在曼哈顿中城

sentences.en: Manhattan office building on Monday was carrying a note that criticized the National Football League, the apparent target of his shooting, and claimed that he had developed
sentences.zh: 一栋办公楼内枪杀四名人员的枪手随身携带了一张纸条，批评了国家橄榄球联盟，这显然是他枪击的目标，并声称自己因这项运动患上了退行性脑病。

sentences.en: a degenerative brain disease from playing the sport.
sentences.zh: 警察说，枪手针对NFL的计划在他进入一个无法通往该联盟办公室的电梯间后被挫败了。

sentences.en: Police said that the shooter's plan to target the NFL was thwarted after he entered an elevator bank that did not have access to the league's offices.
sentences.zh: 警察说，枪手针对NFL的计划在他进入一个无法通往该联盟办公室的电梯间后被挫败了。

sentences.en: And Representative
sentences.zh: 而佐治亚州众议员

sentences.en: Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia, a close ally of President Trump, became the first member of her party in Congress to call Israel's conduct in Gaza a genocide.
sentences.zh: 马乔里·泰勒·格林作为特朗普总统的亲密盟友，成为了国会中她所在政党里第一个将以色列在加沙的行动称作种族灭绝的成员。

sentences.en: In a post on social media,
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体的一篇发文中，

sentences.en: Representative Greene said that the October 7th attacks against Israel were, quote, horrific.
sentences.zh: 格林议员表示，10月7日针对以色列的袭击是，引述，“可怕的”。

sentences.en: But so is the genocide, humanitarian crisis, and starvation happening in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 但加沙正在发生的种族灭绝、人道主义危机和饥荒同样如此。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由

sentences.en: Olivia Natt and Anna Foley.
sentences.zh: 奥利维亚·纳特和安娜·福利制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willans and Brendan Klinkenberg.
sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威兰斯和布伦丹·克林肯伯格剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell,
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔、

sentences.en: Marion Lozano, and Rowan Nemisto, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 马里恩·洛扎诺和罗温·内米スト的原创音乐，并由阿丽莎·莫克斯利进行混音工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonder Week.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由吉姆·布伦伯格和来自奇异周的本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbara.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴拉。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让你的客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是深度睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线环境，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有对什么过敏或饮食禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢收听播客的任何地方查找《Wirecutter秀》。

sentences.en: to take a look around and share it.
sentences.zh: 四处看看并分享它。
